name: Vadugeeswarar Temple, Thiruvandarkoil (Thiruvadugur)
deity: Shiva as Vadugeeswarar (Panchanatheeswarar), with the Goddess Thiripurasundari (Vadugur Nayaki)
period: A Paadal Petra Sthalam of Nadu Nadu, the Thiruvadugur of the Tevaram, sung by Sambandar (7th century); Chola inscriptions
summary: On the road between Villupuram and Puducherry, the Thiruvadugur of Sambandar's hymn keeps the memory of Vaduka Bhairava, who worshipped the Lord here after slaying the demon Mundasura.

sections.history: Thiruvandarkoil is a village in the Union Territory of Puducherry, on the highway from Villupuram, about 21 km to the west, and it is the Vadugur — Thiruvadugur — of the Tevaram. Its temple is one of the 276 Paadal Petra Sthalams and is counted sixteenth among those of Nadu Nadu; Thirugnana Sambandar sang its Lord in a pathigam preserved in the first Tirumurai. The stone carries the record of the Cholas: inscriptions of Rajaraja I, Kulothunga I and Rajendra III are found on its walls. The temple is today a protected monument in the care of the Archaeological Survey of India.
sections.architecture: Unlike most Tevaram shrines, the temple has no gopuram: it is entered through a simple east-facing gateway in its compound wall, and the old Chola masonry stands without later towers to hide it. The Lord is worshipped as a lingam in the sanctum. The Goddess, Thiripurasundari, also called Vadugur Nayaki, has her own shrine and is portrayed with the attributes of Mahalakshmi, and Vaduka Bhairava, whose story gives the temple its name, is honoured within.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells of the demon Mundasura, who tormented the world until Shiva sent Vaduka Bhairava, one of the eight Bhairavas, to destroy him. Though the demon was slain for the good of all, the killing left its stain, and Bhairava came here to worship the Lord and be cleansed of it. The Lord who received his worship became Vadugeeswarar, the Lord of Vaduka, and the village took the name Vadugur — the Thiruvadugur of Sambandar's hymn.
sections.festivals: Bhairava receives special worship on the Ashtami of the month of Karthigai, the day sacred to him, and a one-day festival is kept in the month of Chithirai. Maha Shivaratri and the monthly pradosham are observed as at every Shiva shrine; confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: Thiruvandarkoil is an easy stop between Villupuram and Puducherry, and its plain, towerless walls give it an air of great age. Devotees of Bhairava come especially on Ashtami days, and Tevaram pilgrims pair it with the other Nadu Nadu shrines of the Villupuram country.

visit.timings: Open daily in morning and evening sessions with a midday closure. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left outside before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is not permitted inside the sanctum. As a protected monument, the temple may have its own rules for photography of the structure; ask the staff before taking pictures, especially of rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Thiruvandarkoil lies on the Villupuram–Puducherry highway, about 21 km east of Villupuram and about 20 km west of Puducherry town, with frequent buses on the route. Villupuram is the nearest major railway junction and Puducherry also has a station; Chennai is the nearest major airport, with Puducherry's small airport closer at hand.
